indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: BI.2.1.1: Recognize that some events in our environment occur recurrently
indicator.objective: Explain that some natural phenomena, such as day and night, occur repeatedly

skills.description: Recognise that day and night come one after the other, again and again
Give examples of things seen in the day and things seen at night
Put simple day/night events in the correct order

misconceptions: Day and night happen only once.
The sun goes away completely at night.
The moon only appears on some nights.

questions.stem: What do we see in the sky during the day?
questions.explanation: The sun is seen in the sky during the day.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the moon is only seen at night, but it is sometimes visible in the day too; however, the sun is the main object seen in the day.

questions.stem: What do we usually see in the sky at night?
hints: It is round and gives light at night.
questions.explanation: The moon and stars are usually seen at night.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the moon is always full and bright every night.

questions.stem: After night, what comes next?
hints: When you wake up, it is bright.
questions.explanation: Day comes after night. This happens over and over again.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think night lasts forever.

questions.stem: Which of these activities is done during the day?
hints: What do you do in the morning?
questions.explanation: Going to school is an activity done during the day.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think sleeping is only done at night.

questions.stem: Does day and night happen once or many times?
questions.explanation: Day and night happen repeatedly, over and over again.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think day and night happen only once.

questions.stem: When it is dark outside and you can see the moon, it is...
hints: What time do people usually sleep?
questions.explanation: When it is dark and the moon is out, it is night.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse evening with night.

questions.stem: Which of these comes first in a day?
questions.explanation: Morning comes first in a day.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think afternoon comes before morning.

questions.stem: What comes after evening?
questions.explanation: Night comes after evening.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think morning comes right after evening.

questions.stem: Kofi woke up and saw the sun shining. What time of day is it?
questions.explanation: When the sun is shining, it is day.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse morning with night if they wake up early.

questions.stem: Ama sees stars in the sky. What time is it?
hints: Stars are seen when it is dark.
questions.explanation: Stars are seen at night.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think stars are seen in the day.

questions.stem: What happens every morning?
questions.explanation: The sun comes out every morning.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the moon comes out in the morning.

questions.stem: Write the word that comes after morning.
hints: The sun is high in the sky.
questions.explanation: Afternoon comes after morning.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think night comes immediately after morning.

questions.stem: Why do we say day and night occur repeatedly?
options: Because they happen over and over again
Because they happen once a year
questions.explanation: Day and night occur repeatedly, meaning they happen over and over again in a cycle.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think 'repeatedly' means only twice.

questions.stem: Which of these is the correct order of a full day?
hints: Start with when you wake up.
questions.explanation: The correct order is morning, afternoon, evening, then night.
questions.misconception: Pupils may mix up the order of the day.

questions.stem: If it is night now, what will come next?
hints: What happens when you wake up?
questions.explanation: After night comes day (or morning).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think it stays night forever.

questions.stem: Draw a picture of something you see in the day and something you see at night.

criteria.description: Draws a correct day object (e.g., sun)
Draws a correct night object (e.g., moon, stars)

hints: What is in the sky in the day?
What is in the sky at night?
questions.explanation: This tests the understanding of day and night objects.

questions.stem: Ama says 'Day and night happen only once.' Why is she wrong?
hints: Does it happen today? Did it happen yesterday?
questions.explanation: Day and night happen every day. They are repeated over and over.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not understand the concept of recurrence.

questions.stem: If it is afternoon now, which of these will happen next?
hints: The sun starts to go down.
questions.explanation: Afternoon is followed by evening.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think morning comes after afternoon.

questions.stem: Tell me what happens to the sun and the moon over a whole day.

criteria.description: States the sun comes out in the day
States the moon comes out at night

hints: When do you see the sun?
When do you see the moon?
questions.explanation: The sun is out during the day, and the moon is seen at night.

questions.stem: Which of these happens in a repeating cycle?
questions.explanation: Day and night occur in a repeating cycle.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all daily activities are natural cycles.
